title: Pulled Pork
subtitle: Slow-roasted spiced pork shoulder
excerpt: A whole pork shoulder rubbed in smoked paprika, cumin and garlic, then roasted low and slow for five hours until the collagen breaks down and the meat pulls apart in long, juicy shreds. The result is rich and smoky, with a sticky dark crust on the outside. It serves a crowd and freezes beautifully.
sourceNotes: Pulled pork is a cornerstone of American BBQ, particularly in the Carolinas where whole-hog pit cooking dates back centuries; the slow-and-low method breaks down the shoulder's collagen into silky, shreddable meat.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze pulled pork in airtight containers for up to 3 months. Reheat with a splash of stock.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The rub can be applied the night before and the joint refrigerated uncovered overnight for deeper flavour.

content.text: Do not rush this. The whole point of pulled pork is the long, low cook that turns tough collagen into sticky gelatin. At 150C the pork will be safe to eat after 2 hours, but it won't pull apart until it reaches an internal temperature of around 90C, which takes closer to 5 hours for a 2kg joint. A probe thermometer is the most reliable way to know when it's ready. If you don't have one, prod the thickest part with a fork: when the meat falls apart with no resistance, it's done.

items.prepNote: bone-in or boneless, skin scored if present
crushed into a paste with a pinch of salt

content.text: Heat the oven to 150C (fan 130C / Gas 2). Mix the smoked paprika, cumin, coriander, chilli flakes, garlic paste, honey and olive oil together in a small bowl to form a thick paste. Season with a generous amount of salt.

Rub the paste all over the pork shoulder, pressing it into any crevices or score marks. Place fat-side up in a deep roasting tin. Pour 200ml of water into the bottom of the tin to prevent the juices from burning.

Cover tightly with two layers of foil. Roast for 4 hours, then remove the foil and roast for a further 45 to 60 minutes until the outside is dark and sticky. The internal temperature should read 90C or above.
Remove from the oven, re-cover with foil and leave to rest for at least 20 minutes. This lets the juices redistribute so the pork stays moist when you pull it.

Use two forks to shred the meat, discarding any large fat deposits and the bone if bone-in. Toss the pulled pork with the resting juices from the tin. Serve piled into rolls with coleslaw, or as a meal with rice and greens.

items.symptom: Pork is not pulling apart after 5 hours
items.cause: The joint is larger than 2kg or the oven runs cool
items.fix: Cover again and return to the oven for another 30 to 45 minutes. Check the internal temperature with a probe: it needs to be at 90C or above before it will pull cleanly.

items.symptom: Juices in the tin have burned
items.cause: Not enough water added at the start or the foil was not sealed tightly
items.fix: Add 100ml of water to the tin and scrape up the stuck bits, which become part of the sauce. Next time seal the foil more carefully around the edges.
